summary: Follow-up on the July 22nd incident where inference latency spiked during high-concurrency batch windows. Root cause discussion focused on mixed model variants, KV cache misses after autoscale, and a kernel fallback that increased p99. Agreed mitigations include pinned model variant for sensitive routes, KV cache warm-up, tuning autoscale cooldown, and an ops runbook for on-call. Redwood to provide traces and kernel logs; Zenith to share workload traces for a bounded pilot test.
topics: Dedicated vs hosted routing for critical routes
Security/audit implications and data residency concerns
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-07-30
- Time: 15:00 PST
- Duration: ~42 mins
- Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Blake Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Jordan Lee (Zenith SRE), Maria Alvarez (Zenith CTO), Samir Patel (Zenith Security), Nina Gomez (Zenith Product)

[00:00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep this tight — follow-up from the July 22nd outage. We want to run through the timeline, what we've learned, and concrete mitigations. Priya will share the logs and kernel traces.

[00:00:18] Jordan: Thanks Alex. Appreciate the deep dive. This incident really impacted a few SLAs during our trading batch windows, so we want to be sure there are clear steps.

[00:00:30] Priya: Yeah, quick note — apologies for the messy names in some of the trace files, the auto-export sometimes renames the quantization profiles. I pulled the kernel fallback traces, the autoscale events, and the KV cache miss graphs.

[00:00:50] Maria: Before we jump into logs, can you restate the suspected root cause? We want everyone aligned.

[00:01:00] Priya: Sure. Short version: we saw a cascade — a rapid traffic spike hit one of your high-throughput endpoints, autoscaler spun up new dedicated workers, those workers started cold and didn't have the warmed KV cache. Combined with a small percentage of requests routed to a model variant that didn't have the optimized attention kernels on that GPU type, so we hit a kernel fallback path that increased per-token latency and pushed p99 from ~220ms to >1.2s for a window of about 6 minutes.

[00:01:30] Samir: And that fallback — was it because of quantization mismatch or an incompatibility with your optimized kernels?

[00:01:40] Priya: It's a combination. The model variant used a slightly different config (int8 vs int4 quant profile) and on that particular hardware, the runtime opted for a safe fallback kernel. Also, the KV cache miss rate spiked because autoscale created new instances with empty caches and we had no prefix-caching or warm-up enabled for those nodes.

[00:02:05] Alex: To be clear, the routing policy allowed mixing variants as a fallback; that helped availability but in this workload it worsened tail latency.

[00:02:15] Nina: That's the tradeoff we were worried about — availability vs predictable latency. For trading rules we need deterministic p99, otherwise we can't commit to SLAs.

[00:02:30] Blake: On the CSM side we heard the concern — we can recommend pinning the critical routes to a single verified model variant and reserving Dedicated capacity for those routes so you don't hit cold starts. That will increase cost but should make latency predictable.

[00:02:45] Maria: Cost is OK if performance is guaranteed — we have to measure.

[00:02:52] Jordan: Can you walk through the KV cache warm-up idea?

[00:03:00] Priya: Yes. Two quick options: 1) proactive cache seeding — when autoscale creates a new worker, Redwood can replay recent prefixes from a warm-up queue so the KV cache populates before traffic is routed; or 2) graceful ramp — hold routing until a health check shows cache hit rate above threshold. Both are implementable; seeding is faster but requires the workload sample.

[00:03:30] Jordan: We can provide a 24-hour anonymized sample of the top prefixes.

[00:03:38] Alex: Great, add that to next steps. Also, Priya, you mentioned kernel selection logs — is there a way to pin kernels or force the optimized path?

[00:03:50] Priya: There's no single "pin kernels" switch right now but there are two levers: 1) lock to a model quant/profile that we know has optimized kernels on the target GPU, and 2) adjust the runtime's kernel selection threshold to prefer performance kernels; the latter has been used in other customers but it's slightly riskier if a kernel has a correctness issue.

[00:04:15] Maria: We can't risk incorrect outputs. We prefer sticking to verified quant/profile combos.

[00:04:23] Priya: Understood. We'll produce a recommended model variant manifest that lists model/config combos validated for your Dedicated GPU type.

[00:04:32] Samir: On the security side — are any of these mitigations going to require us to move data off-prem or change KMS? We have strict residency rules.

[00:04:42] Alex: No, nothing requires data to leave your VPC. Warm-up seeding can be done with an anonymized workload inside your network; Redwood agents running in Private mode can perform cache seeding and the control plane only receives health metrics. For KMS, we respect customer-managed keys; nothing changes.

[00:05:00] Priya: We'll also include audit log samples and explain how cache warm-up events show up in the traces.

[00:05:10] Jordan: One thing — during the incident we saw the autoscaler cooldown set to 30s which seemed too aggressive. Could that have contributed?

[00:05:20] Priya: Yes. Short cooldowns can oscillate scale and increase churn; recommended cooldown for your workload is 5-10 minutes given the bursty pattern. We'll share tuned autoscale policy suggestions.

[00:05:35] Nina: Can you quantify the expected p99 improvement if we pin variant + warm-up + longer cooldown?

[00:05:42] Priya: Based on traces, pinning variant removes the fallback kernel hit, which drops p99 from 1.2s back down to ~300ms under the same hardware. Warm-up reduces the cold-cache contribution — another ~50-100ms improvement depending on prefix overlap. Combined, we estimate p99 in the 240-320ms range. We'll provide more precise numbers after we run a small pilot with your sample trace.

[00:06:10] Alex: Noted. Also discussion on routing: consider splitting critical routes to Redwood Dedicated or Private with reserved pools, and keep non-critical on hosted. That hybrid approach gives a cost/perf trade.

[00:06:28] Maria: We like hybrid. Can Redwood guarantee isolation so the hosted routes won't affect Dedicated pool?

[00:06:35] Priya: Yes — Dedicated pools are isolated. We can set strict routing policy so certain routes never fall back to hosted. We'll document the policy and show config snippets.

[00:06:48] Samir: A quick item — for compliance we need proof that fallback routing can be disabled for certain tenant IDs. Is there an existing capability?

[00:06:58] Alex: Yes, we already support per-route routing policies and can disable fallback or cross-region failover for specified tenant IDs. We'll attach examples.

[00:07:08] Blake: Wrap-up on mitigations — immediate: pin model variant for critical routes, increase autoscale cooldown, enable proactive cache warm-up. Medium-term: run pilot with provided workload, tune kernel selection thresholds if needed. Ops: create on-call runbook for rapid rollback to pinned variant.

[00:07:28] Jordan: Sounds good. On timelines: we can get the workload sample by Aug 4. We need Redwood traces and kernel logs by Aug 2 so our infra team can correlate.

[00:07:38] Priya: We'll package traces, the kernel fallback logs, and a recommended manifest by Aug 2. I'll include a short how-to for cache seeding.

[00:07:50] Maria: Also please include cost estimates for reserving Dedicated capacity for those routes — per-hour and monthly.

[00:07:58] Alex: We'll include a comparative spreadsheet (hosted vs dedicated) with estimated TCO for your traffic profile.

[00:08:06] Nina: One last question — competitors were mentioned in our internal review. Are there unique Redwood capabilities for observability compared to MajorCloud?

[00:08:15] Priya: We provide token-level latency breakdowns, kernel selection traces, and KV cache hit/miss heatmaps exported as CSVs. MajorCloud gives some metrics but not the same kernel-level visibility. We'll attach examples.

[00:08:30] Samir: Good.

[00:08:35] Alex: Ok final recap — action items and owners are in the next steps. We'll follow up with a calendar invite for the runbook review week of Aug 9. Blake will coordinate CSM side. Anything else?

[00:08:50] Jordan: No, that's it. Thanks all.

[00:09:00] Meeting end

Notes on transcript quality: some auto-transcription mislabels like "KV cache" as "K V cash" in original logs; product names sometimes shown as "Redwood Dedicate". We preserved natural speech and short crosstalk.
